caseStudy.overview:
Braiding appointments take hours, and many salons still book them through phone calls and direct messages. Awaa Braids lets customers pick a style, see an honest price and how long it takes for the size and length they choose, and request a time that is really free. The salon runs its day from a phone: it confirms, moves or declines requests, manages styles, stylists and hours, and sees its numbers.

It was built in five milestones and is live with a demo salon anyone can try, including a one-minute guided tour.

process.intro: I started from the rules, not the screens: what a booking needs to be fair to the customer and safe for the salon, written and tested in the database first.
steps: Brief: two roles (customer and salon), the booking rules (hours, notice, cancelling, no double-booking) and a phone-first flow.
Data model and security first: Row Level Security and server-side booking, tested with database checks.
Booking in four steps, with free times worked out from hours, time off and other bookings.
The salon's tools: requests, calendar, styles and prices, working weeks and time off, reports.
Notifications from the database, Amharic, offline and accessibility checks (axe) at four widths.
A guided demo tour, a starter salon file and a setup guide for connecting a real salon.

caseStudy.problem: Booking braids by phone call or DM is slow for both sides: the price depends on size and length, a style can take four to six hours, and the stylist's day fills up in uneven blocks. Customers wait for replies and guess at prices; the salon keeps the diary in its head or on paper and risks double-booking.

caseStudy.solution: A phone-first web app with two sides. Customers book in four steps: a style, then size and length with the price and time adding up, then a day and a time that is really free with any stylist or a favourite, then review and send. They can cancel within the salon's rules and are told when anything changes. The salon confirms, declines or moves requests with the customer's number one tap away, sees each stylist's day and week, edits styles, prices, hours and time off, and reads simple reports. Booking runs on the server, which works out the price and time and refuses anything outside the rules, including double-booking.

caseStudy.outcome: All five milestones are live on Vercel with a demo anyone can try and a one-minute guided tour. It is checked by 76 database security checks, 80 unit tests and 109 browser tests at phone, tablet and laptop widths, with automatic accessibility checks (WCAG 2.1 AA) in light and dark mode. Next: connecting a real salon with the starter file and the setup guide.
